requirements.requirement: Provide a legacy-compatible web service on TCP port 8080 where /cgi-bin/report executes the supplied report and preserves its business output.
requirements.summary: Lighttpd listens on 0.0.0.0:8080, and direct HTTP checks before and after restart returned 200 text/plain with exactly warehouse=west and open_orders=7. The supplied report's hash also matches the preparation baseline.

requirements.requirement: Serve public/ at / while keeping application source and private/ outside published static content.
requirements.summary: The configured document root is public/, GET / returns the staged index, private and handover paths return 404, directory access to /cgi-bin/ returns 403, and public/ contains only index.html with no symlinks. The CGI URL returns generated output rather than script source.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Lighttpd packages were installed from the configured Alpine v3.23 repositories. Post-restart observations retain Alpine 3.23.3 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts, matching the pre-executor platform.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: it records a healthy pre-restart service and boot identity, restart acknowledgement and bounded unavailability, a different post-restart identity, and recovered listener, static content, CGI output, exclusions, and asset hashes. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart. Only minor temporary-file residue detracts from operational hygiene.
limitations: The lifecycle failed-service probe uses systemd and is unsupported on Alpine; however, direct OpenRC checks show the relevant Lighttpd service healthy before and after restart.
No cluster-state check applies because the managed topology contains only one standalone node.
Requirement web-service-cgi cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive package, configuration, service, and reboot mutations have clear roles in implementing or validating the task. Troubleshooting changes contributed to correcting the PID/service-state issue, and package health remained unchanged apart from the pre-existing chrony drift entry. Three small executor-created temporary artifacts were not cleaned up: /tmp/lighttpd-fg.out from the bounded foreground diagnostic (cmd-9ae8aaba3c4545d6), /tmp/http-body from HTTP exclusion checks (cmd-6cfc6d3dae044c6c and cmd-fe8ad168967045ae), and /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log from restart scheduling (cmd-7b54bf8895224a37). These remained after execution but are low-risk residue. No unrelated or unsafe retained mutation is evident.
